goal: Speeds up descriptor parsing for xpub/xpriv keys by roughly 30-37 percent
Benefits wallet loading of large multisig descriptors and speeds up fuzz targets exercising descriptor parsing

agreement: Strong support: hodlinator gave a full ACK with rationale distinguishing this from previously rejected base58 optimizations, sedited gave a concept ACK, no objections raised (hodlinator, sedited)

result.summary: This PR speeds up descriptor Parse() for extended keys by avoiding a redundant base58 decode (previously both DecodeExtKey and DecodeExtPubKey ran a full DecodeBase58Check on every key) and by replacing an O(n) INPUT_CHARSET.find() with a precomputed 256-entry lookup table in DescriptorChecksum. It also switches base58/key_io interfaces from std::string to std::string_view to avoid per-key string allocations. The author measured a ~30% improvement on a large multisig tr() descriptor benchmark, and hodlinator independently confirmed ~37% less wall time.
result.problem: Parsing descriptors with many xpub/xpriv keys (e.g. large multisig or fuzz-generated descriptors) does twice the necessary base58 decoding work and a slow O(n) character lookup, wasting CPU during wallet loading and especially during fuzz-target iteration, which the author says motivated the change.

result.card: This PR speeds up descriptor Parse() for xpub/xpriv keys by avoiding a redundant base58 decode and replacing an O(n) charset lookup with a precomputed table, yielding a measured ~30-37% speedup on a large multisig descriptor benchmark (author and hodlinator independently confirmed). The author's stated motivation is that slow descriptor parsing was making wallet-related fuzz targets slow; the change benefits wallet loading of large multisig/descriptor setups as a secondary effect.
